scope: Proposition 3.1 (Reduction to a prepared exterior) of the manuscript “The spacetime Penrose inequality and enclosing area” (preprints/The-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-and-enclosing-area-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9bb0c350914915db), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 10-11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (Ω, g, K) be a smooth one-ended exterior as in Definition 1.1, with compact complement of its coordinate end and with g − δ = O6(r−q ), K = O5(r−1−q ), n − 2 2 < q < n − 2. 10 Assume integrable constraint densities satisfying µ ≥ |J|g, finite ADM limits satisfying E > |P|, and θ+(S) ≤ 0 on every boundary component. Suppose that the full-cut infimum of Definition 1.2 is a = Ag min(S) > 0, and put m = (E2 − |P|2)1/2. There are prepared data (gj, Kj) on the same exterior, with one fixed β ∈ (0, 1), numbers ϵj ↓ 0, and proper diffeomorphisms Φj : Ω −→ Ω equal to the identity near S, such that Pj = 0, Ej −→ m, Φ∗ j g ≤ (1 + ϵj)gj, A gj min(S) ≥ (1 + ϵj)−k/2 a. (3.1) The positive constant cj in Equation (2.1) and the end coordinates may depend on j.
